audit_result.proof_trace: The redirect URL is constructed as `${origin}${next}` where `next` comes from the unvalidated `auth_next` cookie or `?next=` query parameter (L17-18). No check enforces that `next` starts with `/` or excludes `@`, so an attacker-controlled value like `@evil.com/phishing` produces `https://app.example.com@evil.com/phishing`, which all major browsers parse with `evil.com` as the host (RFC 3986 userinfo syntax). The `auth_next` cookie is itself set from unvalidated FormData in `actions.ts:286` (`signInWithDiscord`), giving attackers a second injection point.
audit_result.attack_scenario: Attacker submits `signInWithDiscord` with `next=@evil.com/phishing` (via a CSRF-style cross-site form post), setting the victim's `auth_next` cookie. After the victim completes Discord OAuth, the callback at L151 issues `NextResponse.redirect('https://app.example.com@evil.com/phishing')`, which browsers interpret as a redirect to `https://evil.com/phishing`.

PROP-kintai-v3-st-pre-002.text: auth_next cookie redirect target must be validated against same-origin allowlist.
